description: Step 2 of the six-step resolution procedure: an origin already serving blyg.json at the mount root resolves without further probing.
given: A subscription URL whose path at the same origin already serves a blyg manifest (the sample blyg at https://example.com/blyg/).

expect.outcome: Resolved on the direct probe; identity is the final fetch origin and the mount path is not interpreted.
asserts: The procedure order is normalize, direct probe, feed upgrade, rel probe, conventional-mount probes, RSS fallback.
The direct probe is attempted before any HTML fetch.
Nothing is inferred from the mount path (spec 4).

description: Step 3: a URL that is itself a blyg feed (or a feed-linked page) upgrades to the blyg surface via the feed's <blyg:manifest> hook.
given: A subscription URL whose document is feed.xml, whose channel carries <blyg:manifest> naming the absolute manifest.

expect.outcome: Resolved as a blyg subscription by following the feed's manifest hook; the manifest URL becomes the mount root.
asserts: The feed upgrade runs after the direct probe and before the rel probe.
The <blyg:manifest> value is absolute and names the manifest, per spec 7.
Identity is the final fetch origin, never the manifest's self-asserted site.

description: Step 4: an HTML page advertises its blyg via <link rel="blyg">; supporting an equivalent HTTP Link header is OPTIONAL.
given: A subscription URL returning HTML whose <head> carries <link rel="blyg" href=".../mount/">.

expect.outcome: The rel probe succeeds and resolves to the advertised base plus blyg.json, consuming at most one rel hop.
asserts: The HTML <link rel="blyg"> element MUST be supported.
Supporting an equivalent HTTP Link response header is OPTIONAL.
At most one rel hop is followed.

description: Step 5: when nothing is advertised, the reader probes conventional mount points for blyg.json.
given: A subscription URL returning HTML with no blyg link element and no feed manifest hook.

expect.outcome: The reader tries the conventional-mount probes and resolves if one serves a manifest, otherwise falls through to RSS fallback.
asserts: Conventional-mount probing runs only after the direct, feed-upgrade and rel probes fail.
The whole procedure stays within at most 6 fetches.
Relative surface file names are protocol-fixed (spec 4).

description: Step 6: when no blyg surface is found, the reader falls back to plain RSS (L0) and subscribes in legacy mode.
given: A subscription URL that only serves an ordinary RSS/Atom feed with no blyg namespace.

expect.outcome: The subscription is stored in legacy (L0) mode with the feed URL as identity; content is wrapped per spec 13.6.
asserts: RSS fallback is the last step and runs only after all blyg probes fail.
L0 mode yields no versions, no withdrawal and no archive index for that origin.
The origin identity is the final fetch URL.

description: When every step fails the subscription is not created; the six-step procedure terminates in bounded failure.
given: A subscription URL that returns no blyg surface and no usable RSS feed.

expect.outcome: Resolution fails with a surfaced error and no subscription is recorded.
asserts: All six steps were attempted in order within the fetch budget.
The failure is surfaced to the user rather than silently stored.
No partial subscription state is persisted.

description: Subscription identity is the final fetch origin, never the manifest's self-asserted site; the mount path carries no meaning.
given: The sample blyg served at https://example.com/blyg/ whose manifest asserts site=https://example.com/blyg/.

expect.outcome: Identity is the final fetch origin (https://example.com/blyg/); readers infer nothing from the /blyg/ mount path.
asserts: Readers MUST NOT infer anything from the mount path.
Identity is the final fetch origin, not the asserted site.
Ids are scoped to that origin.

description: When the manifest's self-asserted site disagrees with the fetch origin, the reader surfaces it and does not adopt the asserted value.
given: A manifest fetched from one origin whose site key names a different origin.

expect.outcome: The disagreement is surfaced to the user; the fetch origin remains the identity.
asserts: The self-asserted site is advisory only.
The asserted value MUST NOT be adopted as identity.
Existing state is never silently re-scoped.

description: Redirects are bounded (recommended 5) and the final URL wins as the origin.
given: A subscription URL that redirects several times before serving a manifest.

expect.outcome: The reader follows a bounded number of redirects (recommended 5) and adopts the final URL as the identity origin.
asserts: The redirect chain is bounded; an over-long chain fails resolution.
The final URL after redirects wins as the origin.
Each hop counts against the fetch budget.

description: Adopting a new origin for an existing subscription is an identity change and MUST be user-confirmed, never automatic.
given: An existing subscription whose re-resolution now lands on a different final origin.

expect.outcome: The reader prompts the user to confirm re-pointing the subscription; nothing changes until confirmed.
asserts: Origin changes are surfaced as identity changes.
No automatic re-scoping occurs.
Declining leaves the previous identity and state intact.

description: Polling uses conditional requests and honors 304 Not Modified.
given: A stored subscription with an ETag and Last-Modified from a prior poll.

expect.outcome: The next poll sends If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since and treats a 304 as 'no change', mutating nothing.
asserts: Conditional headers are sent when the stored validators are present.
A 304 leaves stored state unchanged.
A changed response advances reconciliation.

description: Polling backs off exponentially, honors Retry-After, and never tightens the interval in response to failure; failure never discards stored state.
given: Repeated poll failures including a 429 carrying Retry-After.

expect.outcome: The interval grows (honoring Retry-After), never shrinks on failure, and stored items are left untouched.
asserts: Backoff is exponential between attempts.
Retry-After is honored when present.
A poll failure MUST NOT mutate stored item state.

description: Readers send an identifying User-Agent on fetches.
given: Any reader-initiated fetch during resolution or polling.

expect.outcome: Every request carries an identifying User-Agent naming the reader.
asserts: The User-Agent is identifying, not a generic browser string.
It is sent on resolution and polling fetches alike.

description: Fetch hygiene: bounded redirects, response size and time limits, and refusal to fetch private-network addresses.
given: A reader fetching arbitrary third-party URLs discovered from feeds and references.

expect.outcome: Fetches are bounded in redirects, size and time, and requests to private-network addresses are refused.
asserts: Redirect count, body size and total time are bounded.
Private-network / loopback / link-local addresses are refused.
Refusal is surfaced, not retried forever.
